feedback: Repair the conditional compliance-method constraint: the current SPARQL does not enforce “exactly one” permitted method, because two permitted method values pass when no disallowed value exists. For an applicable IA Super/IA ship, require exactly one engineOutputComplianceMethod value and constrain it to the two permitted controlled values (or equivalently detect any count other than one and any value outside that set). Preserve the existing ship target, applicability condition, date datatypes, pre-1-September-2003 construction-stage comparison, delivery/assessment presence checks, and deadline direction.

current_feedback: The applicability constraints are incorrectly unconditional: the NodeShape globally requires exactly one iceClass limited to IA Super/IA and globally requires constructionStageDate, deliveryDate, and assessmentDate. This makes non-IA ships fail a requirement that applies only to IA Super/IA ships, and it imposes date existence outside the applicable branch. Preserve the applicable-branch checks, but move the IA/IA Super selection and required date/evidence checks into conditional logic so non-applicable ships pass without these requirements. Also retain the prior repair: for an applicable ship, enforce exactly one engineOutputComplianceMethod value and require that value to be one of the two permitted controlled methods.

Do not make the IA/IA Super restriction global, and do not allow missing iceClass to select the non-applicable branch. Preserve the prior exact-one method repair, date datatypes, construction-date direction, and assessment-deadline direction.
